summary: A task commit carries what the index says and the verdict it was measured under. commit-task-work, commit-audit-state and commit-manifest-index share one staging sequence in _scoped_commit: a staged rename or deletion commits both halves, a tracked file or directory under an ignore rule is staged without -f, an ignored untracked path is named, every refusal after staging puts the allowed paths' index entries back as they were found, every commit uses a pathspec, and the one commit made from an index is built in a temporary index and still runs the project's hooks. The commit is bound to the task's newest gate verdict: passed and current for a declared scope normalised once on both sides (line ranges stripped, directories expanded, the plugin's own record paths excluded), measured under the gate declared now (a digest of the resolved gate), a red retired only by a green or a journaled --override-verdict, and a cleared task bound on its empty-gate record. The task-or-phase gate rule has one home, _manifest_io.gate_entries, read by every surface. Reviewed twice, every finding fixed; merged with main before the gate; phase gate green with the tree unchanged; the invariant check found no breach. P71.1 itself was committed by hand while its recorded gate was red from an unrelated open bug - the case this phase now refuses without an override.

tasks.title: commit-task-work commits a staged rename's source, stages tracked files under ignored directories, and is bound to the task's newest verdict
tasks.description: Field report on 3.0.1, reproduced at HEAD: (1) tracked() asks the index only; after git mv the old path is only in HEAD, so the red-first skip drops it and the commit records a copy. Tracked = index OR HEAD; a HEAD-only path stays out of the git add argv (git add -- old fails 128) and in the git commit -- pathspec (records the rename). Cases for a staged R and a staged D. (2) git add -- <tracked file under an ignored dir> exits 1 AND stages it (git 2.50.1); the script refuses and leaves it staged, breaking 'a refusal leaves the index as found'. Split by ls-files: tracked -> git add -u --, untracked -> git add --; the ignore refusal survives only for untracked paths, named 'ignored; -f is yours to decide'; any failure after staging resets the allowed paths; an untracked declared file under an ignored dir is named, not 'nothing uncommitted'. Never add -f. (3) the commit ignores task.testEvidence: refuse unless the task's newest evidence row is passed and current for the staged work (the declared-work digest run-test-gate records matches what is staged); an explicit override flag writes a journal row. No runtime related-tests step.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_commit_task_work.py: repro that FAILS on current code - a declared path staged as the source of a rename is skipped, so the commit adds the new file and leaves the old one tracked

outcome.technical: Paths only in HEAD stay in the commit pathspec; add -u for index entries with the index restored on failure; the newest evidence row must be passed with a matching declared-work digest, --override-verdict journals the exception.
outcome.descriptive: A task commit records renames and deletions, stages tracked files under ignored directories, and refuses work whose newest gate verdict is not passed.

tasks.description:

An entry with a ':line-range' suffix, or a directory entry, hashes as None ('missing') at gate time AND at commit time, so field_state answers AGREES whatever happened to the file. Probed: owns=['src/a.py:10-20'] and owns=['src'], changing src/a.py -> 'agrees', basis '1 declared file(s); 0 read, 1 missing'. The command then prints that the digest matches, which is false. -> Normalise the scope ONCE in _tree_stamp and use it on both sides (run-test-gate's tested_state and commit-task-work): strip the line suffix (_vocab._strip_line_suffix), expand a directory into the files git lists under it; or refuse UNANSWERABLE when an entry that exists on disk hashed None. Cases for a suffixed entry and a directory entry edited after a green gate, red first.
R2 (med) commit-task-work.py verdict_binding; run-test-gate.py _record_run -> _evidence_io.write_pointer: --record takes the scopeDigest inside run_gate, then write_pointer writes task.testEvidence into the phase file (the manifest itself in the single-file layout) and write_evidence_since also writes the manifest. A task declaring its own manifest/phase file is always MOVED and refused; re-running the gate rewrites the pointer again, so --override-verdict is the only way out. -> Leave the plugin's own record paths (the phase file / manifest, evidence and journal dirs) out of the scope digest on both sides, as reuse_identity already does for the content identity; or digest that file with the pointer block removed. Case: a single-file-layout task that declares audit-plan.json.
R3 (med) commit-task-work.py verdict_binding (the 'if not entries' early return): The empty-gate check returns no-gate before the ledger is read: a task with a newest FAILED row whose gates are later emptied commits without an override, and the NO_GATE sentence says the recorder 'writes no verdict for it' while a red one sits in the ledger. Separately the row's gate is never compared with the gate declared now: a passed row measured under an older/narrower tests.gate still binds after the gate is widened. -> Read the task's rows before deciding no-gate; a newest row is graded (or at least named). Compare the row's gate (step names / declared_gate over current entries) with gate_entries now and refuse on mismatch. Cases: red-then-emptied, gate-changed-after-green.
R4 (med) plugins/audit/reference/execute-task.md step 4c; commit-task-work.py: 4c's exit-1 remedy for a foreign staged path is 'declare them with /audit:task scope'. The doc does not say a scope change after the gate forces a re-measure. -> Tell a list change from a content change (record the declared scope in testedState or derive it from scopeBasis) and word each refusal; add to 4c that widening scope after the gate means recording the gate again.
R5 (med) plugins/audit/tests/test_commit_task_work.py: Branches with no case: _in_head's unborn-HEAD arm; index_snapshot's write-tree refusal (unmerged index); INDEX_NOT_RESTORED; override_row failing after the commit (exit 1 with the SHA); the unreadable-ledger refusal; a reused row whose source is missing; the UNANSWERABLE and NOT_DECLARED arms; '--override-verdict was given and not needed'. -> One case per branch, each fixture telling its branch apart from its neighbours; prove each red by mutating the branch.

A fix, but the CHANGELOG credits commit-task-work only and no case pins it for the other two. -> CHANGELOG line for the other two; one case each in test_commit_audit_state and test_commit_manifest_index.
R8 (low) commit-task-work.py index_snapshot/restore_index; PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md; execute-task.md: Docs say the index is restored 'exactly as it was found', but write-tree drops intent-to-add entries (' A ita' becomes '?? ita') and refuses an index with unmerged entries, so a conflict resolved in the tree but not added - which plain git add used to resolve - is now refused. tasks.title: A cleared task commits on its recorded empty-gate row, and the cleared rule is pinned where it now lives
tasks.description: Merging P70 into this branch put two rules side by side. P70 records an EMPTY gate (a task gate cleared on purpose, or an empty phase gate) as an empty-gate row and pointer under --record, so a done cleared task does not trip no-test-evidence. This branch's commit binding reads the ledger before a no-gate answer and refuses when the newest row is not passed - so a cleared task whose newest row is exactly that empty-gate record is refused, and the only way on is --override-verdict. The empty-gate row IS the recorded answer for a gate that is empty now: accept it there (and only there - an empty-gate row under a gate that has entries now is a gate changed after the measurement, which the gate-mismatch refusal already names). Also pin _manifest_io.gate_cleared / gate_entries' cleared arm with its own cases, since the merge moved it there.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_commit_task_work.py: repro that FAILS on current code - a task whose gate was cleared, with its empty-gate row recorded, is refused by the commit binding

outcome.technical: verdict_binding accepts an empty-gate row while the gate is empty and refuses it as a changed gate otherwise.
outcome.descriptive: A task whose gate was cleared on purpose can be committed on the record of that empty gate.
